blocks.text: Data Quality covered problems that are genuinely visible once you look for them, a missing value count, a duplicate row, an implausible age. Data leakage is a genuinely sneakier failure mode, a dataset can pass every single quality check from the previous topic and still be quietly broken in a way that only shows up once a model is already trained and deployed.

This topic covers what data leakage genuinely is, the main forms it takes, target leakage, train test contamination, temporal leakage, and duplicate leakage, how a suspiciously good result is often the first real clue something has leaked, and the disciplined splitting habits that genuinely prevent it, setting up the Train Validation Test Split topic that follows directly after this one.
1. What Data Leakage Genuinely Is
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993383-309833305.png

Data leakage happens when information that would genuinely not be available at the moment a real prediction needs to be made accidentally makes its way into the training data. The model then learns to rely on that information, performs suspiciously well during testing, because the leaked information is still present there too, and then fails in the real world, where that same information genuinely does not exist yet.

This is a fundamentally different kind of problem from the missing values and duplicates covered in the previous topic, leaked data looks completely normal, it is not missing, not obviously wrong, not inconsistently formatted. The problem is not with the value itself, it is with when that value would genuinely be available in the real world.
2. Target Leakage: When a Feature Is Secretly the Answer

blocks.alt: Target Leakage: When a Feature Is Secretly the Answer
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993383-308014253.png

Target leakage happens when a feature is derived from, or only genuinely exists because of, the very outcome the model is trying to predict. Predicting whether a loan will default, and including a feature called amount written off, is a classic, genuinely real example, that feature only exists once a default has already happened, so a model trained on it looks remarkably accurate while actually just detecting its own answer already sitting in the data.

This kind of leakage is genuinely dangerous precisely because it is subtle, the feature is not labeled target or answer, it has an innocuous sounding business name, and it takes a real, deliberate audit of when each feature genuinely becomes available to catch it before it corrupts an entire model.

blocks.title: A useful audit question
blocks.content: For every single feature, genuinely ask, would this value actually be known at the exact moment a real prediction needs to be made. If the honest answer is no, that feature is a genuine leakage risk and should be removed.

blocks.text: 3. Train Test Contamination
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993384-907457937.png

A genuinely common, easy to make mistake happens during preprocessing itself, fitting a scaler, an encoder, or any other transformation on the entire dataset before splitting it into training and test sets. Doing this lets statistics from the test set, its mean, its range, its categories, genuinely leak into the transformation applied to the training set, even though the actual target values were never directly touched.

The fix is genuinely simple once understood, split the data first, then fit every transformation only on the training portion, and apply that same already fitted transformation to the test portion afterward, never refitting on the test set itself, a discipline covered in real depth in the next topic in this module.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Wrong Order","Genuinely Correct Order"],"rows":[["Fit transformation on the whole dataset, then split","Split first, fit transformation only on the training set"],["Refit a scaler on the test set separately","Apply the training set fitted scaler to the test set unchanged"]]}

blocks.text: 4. Temporal Leakage
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993384-520491259.png

This form connects directly back to the Time Series Data topic earlier in this module, temporal leakage happens when a value that genuinely only exists after a certain point in time is used to predict something at or before that same point. Using next month sales figures to predict this month demand is a genuinely impossible task to replicate in the real world, at prediction time, next month has simply not happened yet.

This is exactly why the earlier topic insisted that a time series must be split by time, training on the past and testing on the future, never randomly, a random split of time series data genuinely creates temporal leakage almost automatically, letting the model see future values while predicting the past.
5. Duplicate Leakage
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993384-193571968.png

If the exact same record, or a near identical one, ends up in both the training set and the test set, the model genuinely gets a chance to simply memorize that specific record during training, and then appears to predict it correctly during testing, not because it genuinely learned a real pattern, but because it has genuinely already seen that exact answer before.

This form of leakage connects directly to the duplicate detection habits covered in the previous Data Quality topic, deduplicating a dataset before splitting it into train and test is not just a general cleanliness habit, it is a genuinely necessary safeguard against this specific kind of leakage.
6. A Worked Example
A small, genuinely realistic loan dataset shows target leakage hiding in plain sight, a feature that looks like an ordinary column but is actually a disguised version of the answer.

code.content:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "loan_amount": [10000, 5000, 20000, 8000],
    "credit_score": [720, 610, 680, 590],
    "amount_written_off": [0, 1200, 0, 3000],
    "defaulted": [0, 1, 0, 1],
})

# amount_written_off is only ever nonzero when a default already happened.
# It is genuinely a disguised version of the target, not a real predictive feature.
print(df[["amount_written_off", "defaulted"]])

blocks.text: Dropping amount_written_off before training is genuinely the correct move here, keeping it in would let the model achieve a suspiciously high accuracy by essentially reading the target off a disguised copy of itself.
7. Suspiciously Good Results as a Genuine Warning Sign

blocks.alt: Suspiciously Good Results as a Genuine Warning Sign
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993385-103592358.png

One of the most genuinely reliable practical signs of leakage is a result that seems too good to be true, a model reporting near perfect accuracy on a genuinely hard, real world problem should prompt real suspicion rather than celebration. Most real prediction problems are genuinely difficult, and a model that appears to have solved one almost perfectly is more often leaking information than genuinely brilliant.

This is worth internalizing as a habit that carries forward into the Model Evaluation modules later in this course, an unusually strong result is not automatically good news, it is genuinely a prompt to go back and audit the data and the pipeline for exactly the kinds of leakage covered in this topic before trusting the number at face value.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: The instinct to celebrate a near perfect result should genuinely be replaced with the instinct to investigate it. Leakage is a far more common explanation for suspiciously strong results than a genuinely superior model.

blocks.text: 8. Preventing Leakage: A Genuine Discipline, Not a One Time Check

Every form of leakage covered in this topic shares a genuinely common fix, respect the real order of time and information. Split the data into training and test sets first, before any transformation is fit. Fit every transformation only on the training portion. Apply that same fitted transformation to the test set without ever refitting it there. Audit every feature for whether it would genuinely be available at real prediction time, not just whether it happens to be present in the historical dataset.

None of these steps are genuinely complicated on their own, the difficulty is habitual, consistently applying them on every project, especially under real deadline pressure when skipping a check feels tempting. This discipline is exactly what the next topic in this module formalizes into a repeatable, genuinely reliable procedure.

blocks.text: 9. Data Leakage Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Data Leakage Versus What Comes Next
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993385-647884793.png

This entire Data Collection and Understanding module has been building toward one genuinely practical destination, a dataset that is properly shaped, properly sourced, quality checked, and free of leakage, ready to actually be split and used. The next, final topic in this module makes that last step explicit and rigorous.

Train Validation Test Split covers exactly how to divide a genuinely clean dataset into the pieces a real machine learning workflow needs, and it directly incorporates every leakage lesson from this topic, splitting before fitting, respecting time order, and removing duplicates first.

items: Data leakage happens when information unavailable at real prediction time accidentally enters training.
Target leakage: a feature that is secretly derived from or dependent on the target itself.
Train test contamination: fitting a transformation on the whole dataset before splitting it.
Temporal leakage: using genuinely future information to predict something in the past.
Duplicate leakage: the same record appearing in both the training and test sets.
A suspiciously perfect result is a genuine warning sign of leakage, not automatically good news.
Prevention is a consistent discipline: split first, fit only on training, respect time order, deduplicate first.
